faq.q: What is the average temperature in Marbella in April?
faq.a: Daytime highs reach 20-22°C, with overnight lows around 12-14°C. Sea temperature sits at 16-18°C, so swimming is brisk but doable with a wetsuit or on sunny afternoons.

faq.q: Is April a good month for a yacht charter in Marbella?
faq.a: Yes — April offers mild weather, fewer crowds than summer, and lower prices on some boats. Winds are steady but not rough, making it suitable for both motor and sailing charters. The Golden Mile and Puerto Banús are quieter, so you get a more relaxed experience.

faq.q: What should I wear for a April yacht charter in Marbella?
faq.a: Layers are key: a light jumper or windbreaker for the morning, shorts or a dress for midday. Bring a sun hat, sunscreen (SPF 50), and sunglasses. Non-slip shoes are recommended on deck. A light jacket is useful for the return trip as the breeze picks up.

faq.q: Which boats are best for April weather conditions?
faq.a: Flybridge yachts like the Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) offer sheltered upper decks if it’s windy. Enclosed saloon boats like the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) let you stay warm while enjoying sea views. For smaller groups, the Fairline Targa 12m (12m, 10 pax) has a good cockpit cover.

faq.q: Does it rain much in Marbella in April?
faq.a: April sees on average 2-3 rainy days, with total precipitation around 30-40mm. Showers are usually brief and pass quickly. Most days are sunny or partly cloudy, so rain is unlikely to disrupt your charter. Check the forecast 48 hours before departure.

faq.q: What are the wind conditions like for sailing in April?
faq.a: Typical wind speeds are 8-15 knots, with occasional gusts up to 20 knots in the afternoon. The Poniente (west) wind is common, bringing clear skies. This is ideal for sailing boats like the Lagoon 380 (11.6m, 10 pax) or motor yachts with stabilizers.

faq.q: How many hours of daylight do I get in April?
faq.a: You get approximately 8.5 to 9 hours of usable daylight, with sunrise around 07:45 and sunset near 20:30. The best charter slot is 11:00-17:00 when the sun is highest and temperatures peak. Late afternoon light is beautiful for photos along the coast.

faq.q: Can I swim in the sea in April in Marbella?
faq.a: Yes, but the water is cool at 16-18°C. Many guests do take a quick dip, especially after a few hours of sun. If you plan to swim, bring a wetsuit or choose a yacht with a heated deck shower. Cala del Faro and Cala Cortés are sheltered spots with calmer water.

data.body_html:
April 2030 in Marbella delivers some of the most pleasant spring sailing conditions on the Costa del Sol. With daytime temperatures averaging 20-22°C, sea breezes of 8-15 knots, and 8-5-9 hours of daily sunshine, it is an excellent month for a yacht charter in Marbella. The water is still cool (16-18°C), but the sun warms the deck quickly, and the lack of summer crowds means you can enjoy Puerto Banús and the coastline with more space and lower prices on select boats.

April Temperature and Sunshine Hours

Average high temperatures in Marbella during April range from 20°C early in the month to 22°C by the end. Overnight lows drop to 12-14°C, so bring a light jacket for evening returns. Sunshine hours increase from 8 hours early April to 9 hours by late April, with sunset around 20:30. The UV index is moderate (5-6), so sunscreen is still essential. The sea temperature hovers at 16-18°C — refreshing but not freezing. For a warmer experience, book a charter between 11:00 and 17:00 when solar gain is strongest.

Wind and Sea Conditions for Sailing

The prevailing wind in April is the Poniente (west), bringing clear skies and moderate gusts. Typical speeds range from 8-15 knots, occasionally reaching 20 knots in the afternoon. This is ideal for both motor yachts and sailing catamarans like the Lagoon 380 (11.6m, 10 pax). The Mediterranean remains relatively calm, with wave heights of 0.5-1.2 metres. If you are prone to seasickness, choose a yacht with stabilisers such as the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) or the Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax).

Best Boats for April Weather

For April, we recommend boats with covered decks or enclosed saloons to maximise comfort. The Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax, €4,719 minimum 4h) offers a spacious saloon and a large flybridge with sun protection. The Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) has a sheltered upper helm and plenty of seating. For smaller groups, the Fairline Targa 12m (12m, 10 pax) provides a good cockpit cover. If you want a sailing experience, the Lagoon 380 (11.6m, 10 pax) handles April winds well. All charters include a licensed skipper, fuel, drinks, and snacks.

Where to Cruise in April

April’s mild weather is perfect for exploring the coast from Puerto Banús east to Cabopino or west to Estepona. The Golden Mile offers sheltered waters close to shore. Cala del Faro and Cala Cortés are two quiet coves where you can anchor for a swim or lunch. If you want a longer trip, head to Sotogrande (about 20 NM west) for its marina and golf courses. The sea state is usually calm enough for a smooth ride, even on smaller boats like the Mariah SX21 (6.4m, 5 pax).

What to Pack for an April Charter

Layers are essential: a light jumper or windbreaker for the morning, shorts or a dress for midday, and a jacket for the return. Non-slip shoes are recommended. Bring a sun hat, SPF 50 sunscreen, and polarised sunglasses. A swimsuit is optional — the sea is cool but swimmable on sunny afternoons. If you plan to fish or snorkel, the visibility is good in April, around 10-15 metres in calm conditions.

Booking Tips for April 2030

April is a popular spring month, especially during Easter and school holidays. Book at least two weeks in advance to secure your preferred yacht and time slot. Tier A boats like the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) cost €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for 8 hours (skipper, drinks, VAT included). The Mangusta 80 starts at €4,719 for 4 hours and includes a free jet ski. For other boats, contact us via WhatsApp for pricing and availability. All charters include a licensed skipper, fuel, insurance, and Spanish IVA (21%).
